newsitem.title: USA: Ukraine deputy pm sees EFF fixed this month.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine deputy pm sees EFF fixed this month.

text.p: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk said Tuesday he expected final details of an Extended Fund Facility loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund to be resolved this month.
"There is a small group of issues to be solved during the next mission of the IMF to Kiev," Pynzenyk told Reuters through an interpreter.
Asked when the details would be fixed, he said "this month."
Ukraine has been in talks with the fund over a $2.5 billion to $3 billion EFF.
"Two missions have visited Kiev from the IMF, and we have agreed on the major parameters for the EFF. The majority of issues have been agreed upon," Pynzenyk said.
The IMF last week agreed to extend the latest installment of the $867 million standby credit.
Asked if Ukraine wanted a $1.5 billion stabilization fund, which has been under discussion, for its new hryvnia currency, he said Ukraine had not officially sought it.
"We considered and continue to consider that the best stabilization fund will be our stable economic policy," Pynzenyk said.
